title: Exemplar performance signature publish pipeline for verified model profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: New model onboarding lacks a lightweight, auditable pipeline that emits a compact performance signature (latency P50/P95, throughput for common batch sizes, and normalized cost per 1k tokens) that can be published as a Redwood-verified artifact. Current publish flow is manual, inconsistent between eng squads, and slow to pin versions. Goal: Build an exemplar pipeline that automates benchmarking for a candidate model, generates a signed performance signature artifact, stages it in the profile registry, and exposes metadata for pinning rules and rollback heuristics. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the exemplar pipeline used by model onboarding and the performance catalog team.
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmarking job runs end-to-end for a sample model and emits a JSON signature with fields: model_name, model_version, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, median_throughput_rps, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, measured_sequence_lengths, benchmark_config_id, timestamp
Signature artifact is stored in the profile registry and has an immutable versioned key plus a signed checksum accessible to the Console
Publish flow supports tagging as 'verified-exemplar' and a one-click promote-to-verified action in Console for release engineers
Pinning policy UI reads the signature and suggests pin candidates with clear rollback signals (e.g., +20% latency P95 or +15% cost), and these suggestions surface in a canary rollout config
End-to-end telemetry (benchmark job, publishing job, Console metadata) is tracked in the performance dashboard so regressions are visible within 10 minutes of run completion
tasks: Draft PRD sketch and acceptance criteria (this document)
Prototype benchmark runner harness that accepts standard workload manifests
Define compact performance signature schema and JSON contract with fields and units
Integrate signature publisher with the profile registry API and S3-backed storage
Console: Add verified-exemplar badge and promote flow UI
Create pinning suggestion heuristic and wire into rollout config generator
Add dashboard widgets for signature history and delta comparisons
Write operational runbook for the benchmark jobs and failure modes
notes: Trade-offs: we intentionally keep the exemplar signature compact to avoid storing full tarball artifacts; full benchmark artifacts will remain accessible via linked GitHub/GDrive paths for audit.
We need to coordinate with ENG infra to ensure sandbox quotas for short-lived benchmarking fleets (see ENG dependency ENG-18421).
Cost normalization: use current cataloged GPU hour rates and token normalization rules from finance; example formula in PRD notes.
Consider optional 'fast mode' benchmarking for quick pre-validation that only runs 10% of the full profile using smaller batch sweeps.
Legal/Compliance: signatures should not contain customer data; benchmark datasets must be synthetic or public corpora.
Related docs: Confluence draft https://confluence.redwood/inference/verified-exemplar-pipeline and benchmark harness README https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/exemplar
